name: EV charging hub
summary: DC fast-charging plaza (150–350 kW dispensers) priced per port, including charger hardware, make-ready (switchgear, transformer, conduit), paving and canopy. Charger hardware is ~45–60% of cost; installation cost per charger falls sharply with site size (ICCT: ~$45k for a single 50 kW unit vs ~$18k each at 6+ units), while utility make-ready is the main wildcard (PSEG-LI: $78k–116k per port). Default anchored on 2024 Colorado NEVI awards (~$183–193k total per port); canopy and paving adders are derived.

typicalSize.method: Low 4 = NEVI minimum of four 150 kW ports per site (federal rule, not retrieved here — verify); mid 8 ports typical of newer branded hubs; high 20 = large travel-center plaza. ICCT (e1) projected 67% of DC fast chargers at sites with 6+ chargers by 2025.

primaryUnitsPerAcre.method: Each port needs a ~10×20 ft stall (200 SF) plus share of drive aisle (~200 SF), equipment/transformer pad, landscaping and access ≈ 1,100–2,900 SF of site per port → 43,560 ÷ 1,750 ≈ 25 ports/acre.

parkingPerPrimaryUnit.method: The charging stall itself is inside the per-port hard cost (paving line). Additional parking only where the hub includes a lounge/retail amenity (up to 0.5 extra spaces per port).

perPrimaryUnit.method: Anchored on 2024 NEVI data: e4 Colorado NEVI total project cost $183,116–$192,614 per port (≈5.8 ports/site) × ~0.87 hard-cost share (soft ≈ 15%, see softCosts) ≈ $160–168k hard per port for 150 kW corridor sites, typically without canopies. Add canopy ≈ $10–15k/port → mid $175k. Cross-checks: e5 PSEG-LI utility make-ready alone $77,555 (community) – $116,330 (corridor) per DCFC port (2022) before charger hardware ($75.6k–$150k per e3 RMI 2019); e1 ICCT 2019 hardware+install at 6+ chargers/site $93.6k (150 kW) – $165.7k (350 kW); e2 ICCT 2021 average 150 kW $103,636 — older studies omit utility make-ready, canopy and paving, so they sit below. Low $120k = large 150 kW site with existing service and no canopy (≈ e2 + minimal make-ready). High $280k = 350 kW dispensers ($128–150k hardware, e3) + corridor make-ready (~$110k, e5) + canopy/paving. Evidence years 2019–2024; default expressed in 2024$ (NEVI anchor); older figures used only as cross-checks.

scope.notes: Charger hardware (power cabinets + dispensers), on-site make-ready (switchgear, transformer pad and customer-side transformer share, conduit/trenching, wiring), paving, lighting, canopy, signage, GC/OH&P. Excludes utility line extension beyond the property, utility contributions-in-aid, land, network/software contracts, soft costs.

systemSplit.method: Built from the mid composition: charger hardware ≈ $100k of $175k (~0.57) and electrical installation labor/materials (e1 install split ≈ 40% labor / 60% materials) ≈ 0.05 → 26 = 0.62 (EVSE treated as electrical equipment); transformer/service pad & duct bank → 33 = 0.10; canopy steel 05 = 0.05 with roofing 07 = 0.01; equipment pads 03 = 0.03; paving/striping/bollards 32 = 0.07; grading 31 = 0.03; network/comms 27 = 0.01; general conditions 01 = 0.08. Proportions are estimates (verify).

lineItems.name: DC fast charger hardware (150–350 kW, per port)

cost.method: e3 RMI: DCFC (150 kW) $75,600–$100,000; DCFC (350 kW) $128,000–$150,000. e1 ICCT: networked 150 kW $75,000, 350 kW $140,000. Mid = top of the 150 kW range ≈ blended 150/350 kW mix.

lineItems.notes: Carve-out of the baseline. Distributed-architecture (shared cabinet) systems lower per-port cost.

lineItems.name: DCFC installation labor, materials, permit (6+ chargers per site)

cost.method: e1 ICCT Table 4 totals at 6+ chargers per site: 50 kW $17,692; 150 kW $18,577; 350 kW $25,654. Small sites cost far more (1 charger/site: $45.5k–$66.0k).

lineItems.name: Utility transformer, 1,000+ kVA (customer-funded)

cost.method: e3 RMI Exhibit 1: Transformer (1,000+ kVA) $66,000–$173,000; mid ≈ geometric midpoint. A 8 × 150–350 kW hub (~1.5–2.5 MW) may need two units or a 2,500 kVA unit.

lineItems.notes: Often utility-owned and covered by make-ready programs; remove if the utility provides it.

lineItems.name: Charging canopy (steel, LED lighting), per port

cost.method: Assumed: ~250–400 SF of canopy per port at roughly $40–60/SF installed (fuel-canopy analog). Not sourced — verify with a canopy quote.

lineItems.notes: Solar-PV canopy adds cost; see optional item.

lineItems.name: Utility service extension / line work beyond property line

cost.method: Placeholder: $0 where a utility make-ready program covers it, up to several hundred thousand where feeder upgrades are needed. Verify with the utility service request / will-serve.

lineItems.notes: Off-site; excluded from baseline by definition.

lineItems.name: Battery buffer / demand-charge mitigation storage

cost.method: Small behind-the-meter C&I storage priced above utility-scale (Lazard C&I 1 MW/2 MWh DC $238–445/kWh plus AC/EPC — see battery-storage.json e2). 100 kWh per port assumed. Verify.

lineItems.notes: Used where utility capacity is limited or demand charges are high.

lineItems.name: Credit card reader + replacement/dual connector cable

cost.method: e3 RMI: credit card reader $325–$1,000; cable cost $1,500–$3,500; summed.

lineItems.notes: Dual NACS/CCS cables now common; carve-out of baseline.

pctOfHard.method: e2 ICCT notes planning costs 'in some cases can increase total cost by more than 25%' → high. Mid 15% covers design/engineering, utility applications, permitting, commissioning and PM for a repeatable hub design; low 10% for programmatic rollouts.

softCosts.notes: Excludes network/software subscriptions and utility demand charges (operating costs).

design.method: Utility service design often unknown until late; above typical site-civil norms.

hard.method: e1 notes 350 kW sites may 'require very expensive upgrades' to switchgear/distribution; higher than typical 5% sitework contingency.

perPrimaryUnit.method: All-in hard + soft: low ≈ 150 kW port at a large site with existing service; Colorado NEVI totals $183–193k sit near the middle; high ≈ 350 kW port with corridor make-ready, canopy and transformer (~$280k hard × 1.25 + contingency).

source.title: Estimating Electric Vehicle Charging Infrastructure Costs Across Major U.S. Metropolitan Areas (Working Paper 2019-14)

evidence.quote: Table 2: DC fast Networked 150 kW $75,000; Networked 350 kW $140,000. Table 4 totals, 6+ chargers per site: 150 kW $18,577; 350 kW $25,654. 'at a site with one 50-kW charger, installation costs are approximately $45,000.'
evidence.scopeNotes: Value = 150 kW hardware + installation at 6–20 chargers/site; high = 350 kW at 6–10/site. One port per charger assumed. Excludes canopy, paving, utility-side upgrades and planning soft costs.

source.title: Charging Up America: Assessing the Growing Need for U.S. Charging Infrastructure Through 2030 (White Paper, July 2021)

evidence.quote: the average cost for a 150 kW fast charger in 2030 is $100,416 versus $103,636 in 2021 ... This analysis does not include planning costs, which in some cases can increase total cost by more than 25%
evidence.scopeNotes: Hardware + installation, average across site sizes; excludes planning/soft costs, canopy and utility-side work.

source.title: Reducing EV Charging Infrastructure Costs (Nelder & Rogers)

evidence.scopeNotes: Charger hardware only (per charger) and component costs; installation excluded.

evidence.quote: The per-port cost ranges from $183,116 to $192,614.
evidence.scopeNotes: Total project cost estimates (Paren) for NEVI corridor sites incl. federal share of more than $103,000 per port; likely includes soft costs and make-ready; charger power not stated (NEVI requires 150 kW+).

openQuestions: More NEVI award data (PA, OH, TX, etc.) to broaden the 2024 anchor beyond Colorado; split of NEVI totals into hard vs soft.

Canopy and paving per-port adders are assumptions; a public bid tab for a DCFC plaza would replace them.
